text:
Sleep has quietly become one of the busiest shelves in Indian wellness.

This year several Indian brands launched night-time drinks, powders and chewables built around ingredients like glycine, magnesium and L-theanine, many of them without melatonin. Funding into Indian supplement startups is now estimated at over $500 million, and sleep is where a lot of the new launches are landing.

We think that's good for buyers, as long as the labels keep up. Three things are worth checking on any sleep product.

First, the dose next to each ingredient, not just the ingredient list. Glycine studies, for example, mostly used 3 g.

Second, whether it contains melatonin, and how much. It's a hormone, and US sleep doctors advise against it for chronic insomnia in adults.

Third, whether the brand shows lab reports or only badges.

That's the standard we hold SILT Nights to: 3 g glycine, every dose printed, no melatonin, and a lab report for each ingredient.

What do you look at first when you pick up a supplement?
